subject: Change Order: MSA Exhibit C — Bulk capacity reallocation & pricing variance
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Archimedes Health Procurement <procurement@archimedes.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: change order for bulk capacity reallocation + Exhibit C edits

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Archimedes is shifting a portion of the committed GPU capacity from the Q1 reserved pool into a higher-throughput burst tranche across Q4–Q1 to support your model training window. That requires a short change order to the MSA to: (1) reallocate Exhibit C capacity SKUs, (2) reflect the temporary price variance for burst capacity during the training window, and (3) add a brief implementation schedule for cutover.

Attached is a draft change order (RDW-change-order-draft-archimedes.pdf) that shows the Exhibit C reallocation and the proposed temporary fee ladder for burst usage. Please review and let us know:
- Whether the capacity quantities match your internal runbook (I listed the updated vGPU-hours by week)
- Any comments on the temporary rate table (we proposed a flat +18% premium for burst tier)
- Preferred signer for DocuSign and billing contact for the invoice run

If the redlines look fine, Jordan and I will route to Legal for final MSA crosswalk and then generate a DocuSign envelope. If you’d like, we can also surface an implementation mini-plan in Exhibit A for your infra team to coordinate the cutover dates.

Attachments: RDW-change-order-draft-archimedes.pdf (change order), sample exhibit diff table

Thanks — I’ll follow up next week if I don’t hear back.

–Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0194

From: Priya Malhotra <pmalhotra@archimedes.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@archimedes.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@archimedes.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: change order for bulk capacity reallocation + Exhibit C edits

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the draft. Tom and I reviewed with finance. A couple of items we need clarified before legal will sign off:
1) The +18% burst premium — can you provide an example invoice for the proposed model (we need a sample run showing baseline vs burst consumption and resulting charge)?
2) The draft shifts 25% of the committed capacity; can you confirm there’s no interdependency with our active Dedicated pools (we cannot reduce persistent pools during our pilot)?
3) We redlined a small change to Exhibit C (row-level sku mapping) — sending as an attachment (archimedes-redlines.xlsx).

If you can reply with a short note addressing (1) and (2) and update the change order PDF to incorporate our sku mapping, we can route to legal. Decision timeline: procurement + finance want final redline by Nov 5 for inclusion in our November release planning.

Thanks —
Priya Malhotra
Head of Procurement | Archimedes Health
pmalhotra@archimedes.com | +1 617-555-4410

Attachment: archimedes-redlines.xlsx

- Laura, can you own the legal redline once we incorporate Archimedes' sku mapping? They want signoff by Nov 5 for release planning — aggressive but doable if we prioritize.

I pasted Priya's note below for context. Naomi, please prepare a sample invoice example (one-page) showing a 2-week baseline vs burst run and the +18% impact; we can attach it to the updated change order.

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:37:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: change order for bulk capacity reallocation + Exhibit C edits

Hi Priya / Tom —

Appreciate the patience. Quick summary of updates we made based on your redlines and the internal checks:
- Invoice example: attached (one-page) demonstrates baseline vs burst consumption and shows the +18% premium applied only to the burst tranche. Example invoice stub included in the change order PDF.
- Dedicated pools: Karthik confirmed there is no forced reduction of your persistent Dedicated pools — the change order creates a temporary, isolateable burst bucket tied to your commitment and does not reassign active Dedicated instances. We included a protection clause in the implementation schedule (Exhibit A) to prevent automated deprovisioning during your pilot.
- Exhibit C mapping: we incorporated your row-level sku mapping (from archimedes-redlines.xlsx) into the change order and highlighted the edits for Legal to speed review.

Next steps:
1) Laura (Legal) did a quick pass and requested two minor MSA crosswalk edits (standard liability carveouts and a billing contact field). We added those and updated the PDF.
2) DocuSign: I’ve prepared the envelope — please confirm signer and billing contact. Once confirmed, we’ll send the DocuSign link.
3) Implementation: proposed cutover week is Dec 6–12; if that works we’ll schedule a 30-minute runbook handoff with your infra lead.

DocuSign link (preview): https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abc123
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/4857

Attachments: RDW-change-order-draft-archimedes-final.pdf (includes invoice example)

If that all looks good, please reply with a signer name and billing contact and we’ll send the DocuSign envelope.

Best —
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0194
